summary: Asks the model for claims, checks each one against the facts, and swaps in the safe template claims if any fail.
purpose: Make sure published analysis only states facts that can be verified.
why: The header says it falls back to the template when the model's claims fail, so a bad output never reaches readers.
how: 1) Build the input from facts and cutoff. 2) Call generation with fallback. 3) Run the verifier on the claims. 4) If they pass, return the model's claims. 5) If not, build template claims, verify them, and return them with the model's rejection reasons. 6) If the template also fails, raise an error.
inputs: A provider, a verified request (task, system text, facts, cutoff, tier, template function, optional extra input), and a logging function.
outputs: A verified result with the claims, where they came from (model or template), and any rejection reasons.
risks: The template is trusted to be correct, so a broken template stops the whole item. The output limit is fixed at 800 tokens, so long claim lists can be cut short and then fail.
debug: Read the rejections in the result: each gives a claim number and a reason. If the source is always template, read those reasons. If an error says the template fails verification, fix the template for that task.
